papers.title: Intent Contracts: Taking Tools Away from Agents
reasons: 🎯 temas: LLM, AI agents, adversarial ML
papers.abstract_en: Intent contracts are an authorization interface for tool-using LLM agents in which the planning model holds no tools. For each step it submits a short logged contract: a goal, a verbatim quotation of the user, and scope fields. Code validates the contract, and a small trusted model checks it against the user's words and writes the tool call itself. Provided the validation and dispatch code is correct, every executed call is written by the trusted model, the planner's influence on a call is confined to a contract logged before it, and the trusted side decides how much of a request to carry out. We compare contracts with two reviewers of planner-written commands: one sees only the user's words and the command, the information boundary of a reasoning-blind permission classifier, and one also sees the planner's goal and a checked quotation. With gpt-6.1-terra as planner and GLM-5.3-Flash as the trusted model on three AmPermBench task families, every object changed under contracts is named in the goal of the contract that produced the change; under review the planner names objects in its commands and rarely in its goals. When the planner adds work the user never asked for, contracts complete the user's task in 27/30 runs and the intent-visible reviewer in 16/30, because a reviewer can only refuse a whole command. Contracts do not reduce unauthorized actions. They are indistinguishable from blind review, and once the benchmark's environment terms are clarified, every condition that changes state hits a wrong target in 40-49% of those runs. That error is the planner's choice of objects for an ambiguous reference, which no trusted model here can see the environment to check; telling the executor to decline when unsure does not change it. We evaluate benign over-reach with one pair of models, not adversarial planners. We release the plugin and run records.

summary_es.tldr: Los contratos de intención autorizan a agentes LLM a usar herramientas, separando la planificación de la ejecución para mayor seguridad.
summary_es.problema: Los agentes LLM que usan herramientas a menudo ejecutan acciones no deseadas o no autorizadas porque el modelo de planificación tiene acceso directo a las herramientas.
summary_es.propuesta: Introduce 'Intent Contracts', una interfaz de autorización donde el modelo de planificación solo propone un 'contrato' (objetivo, cita del usuario, alcance) que un modelo de confianza valida y ejecuta.
summary_es.resultados: Bajo contratos, los objetos modificados se nombran en el objetivo del contrato. Los contratos completan tareas solicitadas por el usuario en 27/30 ejecuciones cuando el planificador añade trabajo extra, superando a la revisión visible por intención (16/30). Sin embargo, no reducen las acciones no autorizadas (40-49% de errores en condiciones ambiguas).
summary_es.por_que_importa: Mejora la seguridad y el control en agentes LLM que usan herramientas, asegurando que las acciones se alineen con la intención del usuario y reduciendo la ejecución de tareas no solicitadas.

papers.title: Moving Generality from Model to Modeler: LLM Agents for PHM on a Deployment-Style Benchmark
papers.abstract_en: Coding agents built on large language models (LLMs) now help develop many models published as general solutions. Should generality instead reside in the agent that builds a model for each new task? We examine this question in prognostics and health management (PHM), where every model must work on unseen equipment. Our deployment-style benchmark, NextUnit-Bench, covers 24 public datasets split into 58 folds that hold out units or operating conditions; each agent has two hours to deliver an executable predictor, then run on the hidden units. First, frontier agents outperform AutoML, which reaches less than half the best agent's score, and faithful implementations of published methods on four datasets, of which only 6 of 30 beat the strongest agent's own design; published accuracies, where reproducible, rest on the papers' own conventions, and a single convention, capping the remaining life of test engines, can halve the reported error. Second, the agents' advantage is a design made on each machine's data; once made, a plain-text plan of a few hundred words carries most of the gap between two frontier agents, and given a weaker agent's plan, the strongest agent falls to that agent's level, often to identical predictions. Before touching the data, however, it matters little whose plan an agent carries out, and domain toolkits appear to help neither: what sets the strongest apart is how much it learns from the data. Third, such designs reach only implementers that can execute them: given the strongest agent's designs, a locally deployable open-weight model delivers half as often, even when they are lightened, and scores no higher than without them. Generality, we argue, is not disappearing but moving, from the model to the modeler.

summary_es.tldr: Los agentes LLM superan a AutoML y métodos publicados en el desarrollo de modelos de predicción de fallos, moviendo la generalidad del modelo al agente.
summary_es.problema: Los modelos de predicción de fallos (PHM) deben generalizar a equipos no vistos. Los métodos actuales y AutoML no logran esta generalización de manera consistente, y los resultados publicados a menudo dependen de convenciones específicas no replicables.
summary_es.propuesta: Se propone que la generalidad resida en el agente LLM que diseña el modelo para cada tarea específica, en lugar de en el modelo en sí. Se introduce NextUnit-Bench, un benchmark de estilo de despliegue con 24 datasets y 58 folds, donde los agentes tienen 2 horas para crear un predictor ejecutable.
summary_es.resultados: Los agentes LLM superan a AutoML (logrando más del doble de puntuación) y a implementaciones publicadas (6 de 30 superan al mejor agente). La ventaja principal de los agentes es el diseño adaptado a los datos de cada máquina. Los planes de diseño de los agentes explican la mayor parte de la brecha de rendimiento. La capacidad de aprender de los datos es clave. Los modelos de código abierto locales, incluso optimizados, logran la mitad de las predicciones exitosas que los agentes.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Mover la generalidad al agente LLM simplifica el desarrollo de modelos de PHM robustos y adaptables. Permite crear predictores más precisos y fiables para equipos no vistos, mejorando la mantenibilidad predictiva en la práctica industrial.
